messages:
jia: Heads-up — ran a bunch of end-to-end perf profiles on the 8xA100 cluster with the new kernel selector + KV-shard mapping changes. Seeing a regression on TP+PP mixes when KV is sharded per-TP replica.

sam: Ugh, details?

jia: Short summary: baseline (replicated KV per-GPU) avg token latency ~ 42ms. With TP+PP and per-TP shard (striped) we expected compute savings but observed token latency jump to ~58ms and all-reduce stalls show up in timeline.

omar: Do you have traces? nvtx or nsight snapshots?

jia: Pasted relevant snip below — this is from nsight timeline (trimmed):
```
step 123: forward 18.2ms | KV lookup 2.1ms | allreduce start 0.0ms -> finish 3.6ms | wait kernel 21.4ms | backward compute overlap partial
step 124: forward 17.9ms | KV lookup 1.9ms | allreduce start 0.0ms -> finish 3.8ms | wait kernel 24.0ms
```

michelle: Looks like all-reduce time doubled vs baseline (1.6ms -> 3.6ms). Could be NCCL topology or cross-node collectives? Which NCCL version?

jia: NCCL 2.14.3 (same as baseline). Cluster topology is mixed: 4x GPUs per host on two hosts. Baseline had KV replicated so less frequent cross-host comms. Striped shards forced KV fetches across hosts during beam expansion.

omar: So we introduced more cross-host traffic when a single TP slice needed remote KV pages. That explains all-reduce amplification (contention on rings). Did you measure PCIe vs NVLink hop counts?

jia: Yes — correlation between high hop count (host boundary) and allreduce tail. Also noticed batching heuristic: our dynamic batcher sometimes coalesces requests with different shard affinity which increases remote fetch probability per microbatch.

sam: Two angles: 1) change shard placement to be PP/TP aware (co-locate hot keys with TP shards) or 2) change batching to respect shard affinity (don't mix incompatible requests in same microbatch). Both cost tradeoffs.

michelle: Can we do cheap mitigation first? e.g., a shard-affinity microbatch filter — if >X% of reqs in microbatch require remote KV, split the batch. Low complexity and likely reduces cross-host spikes.

perf-bot: perf-regression detector: KV-shard: +38% median token latency on tp+pp profile, spike count > threshold. Linked profiling report: s3://redwood-perf/profiles/1795000000-kv-shard-slosh/

jia: Agreed — I'll prototype a microbatch affinity check. Also want to test hybrid replication: keep small hot-replica of top-5% keys replicated locally and stripe the rest.

omar: For long term, consider topology-aware allreduce plans: switch from ring to tree for cross-host steps or use NCCL communicator split so intra-host reduce happens separately. Might reduce allreduce-impact.

sam: Also review kernel selector: some kernels assume contiguous KV layouts; when shards are remote we incur extra copies/pin/unpin which can blow up latency. Put a cheap fast-path: if KV lookup remote -> use kernel with async memcpy overlap.

michelle: Action list?
jia: I'll open a small PR for microbatch affinity split + add perf tests. Omar — can you prototype communicator-split plan on staging? Sam — kernel fallback quick change. I'll re-run full profiles after changes.

omar: Yep, i'll try communicator-split tomorrow.

sam: I'll add kernel fallback and a flag to force local-hot-replica.

perf-bot: noted tasks -> create tickets: PERF-3321 (microbatch affinity), PERF-3322 (hot-replica prototype), PERF-3323 (comm-split experiment), PERF-3324 (kernel-fallback).

jia: Thanks — tagging @infra for potential topology info. Will post updated traces when available. :thumbsup:
